extracted.intended_audience: merchants, partners, accountants, and readers of historical Italian commercial law/practice
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examples for forming commercial partnerships: how capital contributions, timing, goods/services, voyage costs, and agreed terms determine how profit and charges are divided among partners. The page gives many worked numeric examples and default rules (e.g., equal shares) for different contribution/timing scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default equal division (equaliter) when no pact
rubrics_metrics.description: If partners make no special pact or conditions, the profit is divided equaliter (equally) among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly states 'equaliter fra loro' and gives examples where, absent specific agreements, the guadagno (profit) is shared equally. Examples illustrate dividing a year's profit equally among partners when no contrary condition is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit entitlement tied to time of capital contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: A partner who adds capital partway through the enterprise is entitled only to the portion of profit accruing from the time their capital was put in (i.e., share proportional to the time their capital was at risk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple worked examples compute amounts 'per il tempo' — months or parts of the year — showing a late entrant receives share only for months after contribution. Numerous numeric illustrations show prorating (months × contribution) to compute each partner's entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit division proportional to capital × time (capital-time method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits are apportioned based on each partner's capital multiplied by the time it remained in the business (so shares reflect both amount contributed and duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript repeatedly forms products like 'capitale × mesi' and divides totals to find each partner's share; many sample calculations (e.g., sums of 200, 300, months, and resulting guadagni) illustrate this standard method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital introduced later yields returns only from its start-date (no retrospective share)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a capital portion is introduced after the beginning, the partner who introduces it receives returns only from the date of introduction — they do not partake in earlier profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples contrast scenarios where one partner puts money at gennaio vs luglio; calculations show that the later contribution participates in subsequent profit only. The text emphasizes computing shares from the insertion point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed fractional or weighted shares allowed by pact
rubrics_metrics.description: Partners may contractually stipulate arbitrary fractional weights or multiple-of-share arrangements (e.g., one partner to receive 3 parts, another 4 parts, another 5 parts) instead of simple equal shares or strict capital-time proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text shows numerous agreements specifying '3 volte, 4 volte' etc., and examples of dividing guadagno per those stipulated multiplicative shares. Guidance: where parties agree specific 'parti' or multipliers, use those to apportion profit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of in-kind contributions (goods, cargo, barrels, merchandise) as capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Goods, cargo, barrels of wine, merchandise, or services rendered can be valued and treated as capital contributions for purposes of sharing profits and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several passages list barrels, vino, mercurio, robba, cargo and show them being valued (in lire or other units) and included in the capital-account computations used to apportion guadagno. Worked numeric examples convert in-kind items into monetary capital-equivalents before apportionment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of voyage/charter and transport costs (nolo, fomento)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter/hire (nolo), freight or voyage-related expenses are handled as charges to be paid and apportioned according to the agreed method (by ratable share, per tariff, or as contracted with the carrier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long examples describe paying the patrone (captain) for nolo, determining how many parties pay which rates, apportioning charter fees across partners or voyages. The text gives step-by-step calculations showing how nolo and other costs reduce net guadagno and how those reduced amounts are shared.

rubrics_metrics.name: When capital and profit are mixed, separate capital return then apportion remaining gain
rubrics_metrics.description: If funds of capital and profit become commingled, first identify and return capital portions; then apportion the remaining guadagno according to the agreed rule (capital-time, equal shares, or contractual fractions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manuscript repeatedly distinguishes 'capitale' and 'guadagno' and shows arithmetic separating capital sums from profit before computing shares. Examples show taking out capitals or accounting for capitals' presence before dividing gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: If parties vary contributions across cycles, recalculate shares per cycle/time-segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnerships that change who contributes (or the amounts) across months or voyages compute shares separately for each time segment and sum results (i.e., treat each period as a mini-partnership for apportionment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text gives many periodized examples (primo mese, secondo, luglio→dicembre, etc.), showing how to compute for each interval according to contributions present in that interval, then aggregate entitlements over the full term.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a partner fails to provide promised capital or terms differ, apply the contract terms or default rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a partner does not fulfil a promised capital contribution or parties stipulate special conditions, the agreed contractual consequences apply; absent mention the default (equaliter or capital-time as shown) governs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are narrative examples and cautions about persons not putting in the agreed sums and how that affects shares: the manuscript contrasts agreed insertions with cases where a partner 'non mette' and shows how to recompute or deny shares accordingly.
